Non-invasive ultra-sensitive detection of breast cancer biomarker using cerium nanoparticle functionalized graphene oxide enabled impedimetric aptasensor

About

Fifteen years between the lab bench and the clinic

I am a biochemist and nanobiotechnologist with more than 15 years of research and teaching experience across India's national research institutes (Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), IIT Delhi, CSIR-AMPRI, AIIMS Bhopal), universities and industry. Since September 2026 I have been an Alexander von Humboldt Experienced Researcher at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, Germany.

My work connects materials science with medicine: electrochemical and optical biosensors for point-of-care testing, 3D-bioprinted and microfluidic tumour-on-a-chip models for drug screening, nanoformulations for targeted drug delivery, and computer-aided drug design. I have led or co-led projects funded by DST, DBT and ICMR, and I hold registered designs and a filed patent application.

Alongside research, I co-founded two ventures, A Fourth Dimension (2021) and Aim Active Life (2025), and in 2025 I was selected for the BIRAC-GIC Women LIFT Health programme.

Research

Diagnostics and models that travel from bench to bedside

Six connected themes, from synthesising nanomaterials to testing drugs on patient-like tissue.

Aptasensor for non-invasive early diagnostics

An aptamer, a short strand of DNA or RNA, is fixed onto an electrode coated with a nanomaterial such as graphene oxide, MXene or metal nanoparticles. When the target biomarker binds, the electrode's current changes in proportion to how much is present. Because the signal is electrical, the reader can be miniaturised to a handheld or smartphone-linked device.

Research areas

E / V → I / µA

Point-of-care diagnostics

Electrochemical, impedimetric and fluorescence aptasensors and immunosensors for cancer, infectious and neurological biomarkers, often from saliva or sweat.

rGO · MXene · QDs

2D & nanostructured materials

Synthesis and characterisation of graphene, MXene, quantum dots and metal or metal-oxide nanocomposites.

µL channels

Organ- & tumour-on-a-chip

Microfluidics, BioMEMS and 3D bioprinting for organoid and breast-cancer spheroid platforms that test drugs on patient-like tissue.

hν → ¹O₂

Drug delivery & phototherapy

Nanocarriers, targeted nanoformulations and photodynamic therapy, now extending to dermatopharmaceutics.

IoT · wearables

Wearable sensors

IoT-integrated, wearable devices for personalised and sustainable healthcare.

ΔG kcal/mol

Computational drug design

Docking, molecular dynamics, network pharmacology, immunoinformatics, and systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
